learning_outcomes.text: Explains the basic principles of heat transfer and the mechanisms of heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation, and uses the fundamental heat transfer equations.
Analyzes steady-state heat conduction in plane, cylindrical, and spherical geometries and calculates heat transfer, temperature distributions, and heat losses using the thermal resistance approach.

Analyzes transient heat conduction and determines temperature variations and heat transfer using the lumped capacitance method and appropriate analytical and graphical methods for one-dimensional systems.
Analyzes heat transfer from extended surfaces (fins) and performs calculations of fin temperature distribution, heat transfer, efficiency, and effectiveness.

Analyzes heat transfer by forced and natural convection using boundary layer concepts and dimensionless numbers, and develops solutions to heat transfer problems using appropriate correlations and engineering calculation methods.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to heat transfer; basic concepts, heat transfer mechanisms, and energy balance
Fundamental principles of heat conduction; Fourier’s law of heat conduction and the general heat conduction equation
One-dimensional steady-state heat conduction through plane walls and thermal resistances
Steady-state heat conduction in cylindrical and spherical geometries
Heat transfer through composite walls; series and parallel thermal resistances and contact resistance
Extended surfaces (fins); types of fins, temperature distribution, and heat transfer
Fin efficiency and effectiveness; fin design and engineering applications
Transient heat conduction; concept of transient conduction and the lumped capacitance method
Transient heat conduction; transient conduction in plane walls, long cylinders, and spheres
Basic principles of convective heat transfer; Newton’s law of cooling and the convective heat transfer coefficient
External forced convection; boundary layers, Reynolds and Nusselt numbers
Internal forced convection; heat transfer in pipes and ducts and the use of appropriate correlations
Natural convection; buoyancy forces, Grashof and Rayleigh numbers, and natural convection correlations
Integrated analysis of heat transfer problems; engineering applications, energy efficiency, and example problem solving
